The world is changing faster than government systems were designed to.
 Governments today face growing complexity, rising expectations and constant change. Yet many of the systems and structures they rely on were designed for a different era.  
 The upcoming report Government Unstuck: The Next Frontier of Government Transformation explores how public administrations can become more connected to citizens, simpler to navigate, more flexible in how they use resources, and better prepared for the future.  
 Drawing on case studies from across #OECD countries, the report highlights the cutting-edge practices that are helping governments strengthen trust, anticipate change and adapt in a rapidly evolving world.  
 Meeting rising expectations will require governments to rethink how they operate, not just expand what they do.
 📅 12 October 2026, 9:15 CEST| OECD Conference Centre, Paris  
 Register for the launch event at the opening session of the 2026 OECD Global Forum on Building Trust and Reinforcing Democracy on #GovernmentUnstuck: https://brnw.ch/21x6jI8

Young people’s mental health has been deteriorating for over a decade.
 Between 2012 and 2022, youth mental health indicators worsened by an average of 3% to 16% annually across nine OECD countries with comparable data.
 What is driving this trend? New #OECD research points to a combination of factors, including socio-economic pressures, bullying, academic stress and the growing influence of digital environments.
 There is no single solution. But stronger prevention, supportive schools and families, and earlier access to youth-friendly mental health services can make a difference.
 On #WorldMentalHealthDay, explore how OECD research can help countries better protect and support young people’s #MentalHealth.
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x6jdq

HCSO SRD Involved in Pursuit Starting at Brainerd High School, Juvenile Suspect Arrested
 Hamilton County, TN – Earlier today, at approximately 3:15 p.m., the HCSO School Resource Deputy assigned to Brainerd High School observed a juvenile female driving recklessly through the school’s parking lot in an apparent attempt to strike an individual with her vehicle. Preliminary evidence indicates that the suspect had targeted this individual that they were attempting to run over.
 The driver failed to stop when the SRD activated their vehicle’s emergency lights and siren, initiating a pursuit. The suspect's vehicle was finally brought to a stop on Shepherd Road, where they were taken into custody.
 The juvenile suspect was arrested and charged with the following:
 -  Aggravated Domestic Assault
 -  Felony Evading Arrest
 -  Driving Without a License
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.title: Halloween Trail Fest Canceled Saturday; Enterprise South Opening Delayed Sunday HAMILTON COUNTY, Tenn.
items.content_text:
Halloween Trail Fest Canceled Saturday; Enterprise South Opening Delayed Sunday
 HAMILTON COUNTY, Tenn. — Hamilton County Parks & Recreation is coordinating with the Office of Emergency Management, the National Weather Service and local meteorologists to prepare for potential impacts from Hurricane Isaias.
 Halloween Trail Fest is canceled Saturday, October 10. Enterprise South Nature Park will open on a two-hour delay Sunday, October 11, allowing staff to assess conditions and address potential hazards, including fallen trees, debris and blocked trails. While conditions may improve throughout the day, the department is taking a cautious approach with public safety as its top priority. Additional closures may be necessary based on conditions.
 “Halloween Trail Fest is a cherished fall break tradition, and our Enterprise South team has invested tremendous time and creativity into this experience,” said Allison Harr, Superintendent of Enterprise South Nature Park. “We share our community’s disappointment; however public safety is our top priority.”
 Visitors are asked to respect the delayed opening and check the Hamilton County Parks & Recreation’s official channels for updates including the Enterprise South Nature Park official Page.

Meet the Emerging Producer!
 Harlan Lovestone is a visual artist, educator, creative producer, and community arts advocate based in Chattanooga. He is the founder of The Art Haus Project, a creative initiative dedicated to using art for good through programs and experiences that strengthen individuals and communities through art, education, and public engagement. On October 14, Harlan will bring the Chattanooga Imagination Fest to Miller Park, creating a day centered around creativity, exploration, and hands-on learning for kids, families, and the broader community.
 Chattanooga Imagination Fest is a family-centered STEAM festival bringing together art, imagination, technology, making, and hands-on discovery. The one-day festival will feature creative build stations, interactive challenges, maker experiences, art activations, and other opportunities for exploration and connection. The festival is being developed with support from River City Company, the Lyndhurst Foundation, and The Art Haus Project.
 In addition to his work as an Emerging Producer, he was also selected for the 2026–2027 Holmberg Arts Leadership Institute and was a 2025 Periscope finalist. His artwork has been exhibited throughout the South and Midwest, with his work as an artist and educator centered on creativity, learning, community engagement, and positive social impact.
 Learn more at www.arthausproject.com and www.chattanoogaimaginationfest.com

items.title: 📢 On the Smart Steps waitlist? CHECK YOUR INBOX! 📩 TDHS has begun sending invitations to apply for child care assistan...
items.content_text:
📢 On the Smart Steps waitlist? CHECK YOUR INBOX! 📩
 TDHS has begun sending invitations to apply for child care assistance, and families have 14 days to respond! ⏰
 If you or someone you know has been waiting for help with childcare costs, please check your email carefully, including your spam and junk folders. An important message like this can be easy to miss!
 ❤️ Please share this post! Someone in our community could miss an opportunity simply because they didn’t see the email in time.
 Childcare assistance can make a life-changing difference for families trying to work, go to school, and provide a better future for their children. Let’s make sure the word gets out!
Progress for Tennessee families! Let’s keep it going.
 The Tennessee Department of Human Services has begun inviting families on the Smart Steps child care waitlist to apply for assistance.
 We welcome this step. For families who qualify, help paying for child care could mean being able to stay in a job, continue their education and give their children a strong start.
 📣 On the Smart Steps waitlist? 
 Watch your email for an official invitation from TDHS Child Care Services. Families who receive an invitation have 14 days to respond and submit an application. Approval depends on eligibility. After the response window closes for the first 100 or so people contacted, TDHS will reach out to the next group of families.
 These invitations are encouraging, and the need remains substantial. According to the Tennessee Commission on Children and Youth, 9,546 families, representing 13,835 children, were on the waitlist as of June 2, 2026.
 Behind those numbers are parents trying to afford the child care they need to work or attend school, and children who could benefit from quality early learning.
 Continued investment in Smart Steps can help more eligible families afford quality child care, keep parents working and strengthen Tennessee’s economy.
 Is your family on the waitlist? We want to hear what waiting means for you. Send us a private message so our team can connect with you. Your experience can help policymakers understand why additional investment matters.
 Together, we can be Loud Voices for Little Kids.

There is something powerful about local childcare providers coming together, sharing their experiences, and having honest conversations about the future of childcare in our community.
 Our providers are more than business owners. They are educators, advocates, and an essential part of the village raising our children. When they come together, we have an opportunity to listen, identify challenges, share solutions, and build a path forward that supports both families and the people who care for our youngest learners.
 The challenges facing childcare are real, but so is the power of collaboration, community, and collective action. We may not have every answer today, but by bringing the right people to the table, we can begin turning conversations into meaningful change.
 This is about more than childcare. It’s about our children, our families, our providers, and the future of our community. The future is worth fighting for, and together, we can build something better. 
 #ChildcareMatters #EarlyLearning

HCSO Assists in Multi-Agency Recovery Operation
 Hamilton County, TN – On the evening of October 7, 2026, HCSO personnel received a report of a suspicious vehicle at the 900 block of Falling Water Trail on Signal Mountain. 
 Deputies discovered the vehicle belonged to a missing person from Norfolk, VA, and initiated a search of the area but suspended it due to safety concerns and it being dark.
 On the morning of October 8, 2026, search operations resumed, and first responders located the vehicle’s owner deceased at the bottom of the waterfall.
 The identification of the individual is being withheld until the family is notified. Please keep this person’s family and loved ones in your thoughts. 
 The HCSO would like to thank the following agencies for their assistance in this operation:
 • Hamilton County STARS
 • Hamilton County Cliff and Cave Rescue Team
 • Hamilton County EMS
 • Hamilton County Medical Examiner Office
 • Tennessee State Park Rangers
 • Walden’s Ridge Fire Rescue
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Helping journalists connect with the people who know and care for this region is an important part of our PR work.
 A new feature in The Independent explores Tennessee’s Indigenous history and the Trail of Tears.
 In May, our team welcomed Scotland-based journalist Robyn Wilson through a hosted visit coordinated with Jill Kilgore and the Tennessee Department of Tourist Development (Tennessee Vacation)'s PR team. During her time in Chattanooga, we joined her for a hike at Moccasin Bend, a boat trip to Williams Island, and an opportunity to learn about Native American history at Audubon Acres
 Two local partners helped make those connections possible:
 • Ava Lowery with Chattanooga Audubon Society shared her knowledge of archaeology and her personal connection to Williams Island, where her grandfather served as a caretaker, and she grew up exploring.
 • Eliot Berz with Tennessee River Gorge Trust guided our boat trip and helped connect Robyn directly with the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, drawing on the Trust’s work with them on signage for Williams Island.
 We’re grateful to Ava, Eliot, Jill, and everyone who shared their time and knowledge during this visit. Their contributions helped Robyn explore this history with greater depth and understanding.
 Read Robyn’s story in the comments below.

items.title: Big news! Head of the Hooch will remain in Chattanooga! 🚣‍♀️ For 22 years, this waterfront has been home to the Hooch,...
items.content_text:
Big news! Head of the Hooch will remain in Chattanooga! 🚣‍♀️
 For 22 years, this waterfront has been home to the Hooch, and we are proud to continue that story here.
 The success of the Hooch has always rested on the dedication of the people who make it possible: our rowers, coaches, volunteers, officials, sponsors, and partners, along with a community that has consistently spoken up for this event.
 When the future of the Hooch was uncertain, you showed up. You shared your stories, wrote emails, spoke with your neighbours, tagged your teams, and made it clear what this regatta means to you, and why keeping it in Chattanooga matters. It's your voice that made the difference.
 After thoughtful discussion, the Friends of the Hooch Board has decided to remain in Chattanooga. We have received the assurances we needed from the city's leadership, along with meaningful commitments regarding the waterfront's development and direct, personal collaboration with the leaders of those efforts.
 Of course, none of this would be possible without partners across our community who came together when we needed it the most.
 We are so grateful for former Mayor and Senator Bob Corker and Ward Davenport, who have been integral in these discussions, and Richard Hardin, owner of the Stone Cup Cafe, who generously stepped forward and offered his unwavering support.
 "My engagement with Kerry and her board has been energizing and rewarding as our two teams diligently produced this outcome. The Hooch is an incredible event and its best days are ahead."
 Bob Corker, former Mayor and Senator
 "It's been really encouraging to watch a public-private partnership evolve and build synergy. It boils down to open communication and will. Everyone at the table saw each resident as a stakeholder, as they should. My hope is that discussions continue between the City, the Hooch, and other event organizers so that both the North and South shores become venues for anything imaginable. The city as a whole won today!"
 Richard Hardin, Owner, Stone Cup Cafe
 The riverfront will take on a new look in the years ahead, with some changes as well as new opportunities for expansion. We will share more details as they are confirmed, and we are confident this community is well placed to navigate the changes together.
 To our rowers and coaches, thank you for making your love for this event known. To our volunteers, thank you for the countless hours you give so that race weekend runs as smoothly as it does. To our sponsors and partners, thank you for believing in the Hooch. And to the Chattanooga residents, business owners, and city leaders who took the time to listen and work with us, thank you for helping make this possible!
 We look forward to seeing you in Chattanooga in one month to deliver the best Hooch yet and begin planning for the future.
 📅 Mark your calendars: Nov 7-8
 #savethehooch #HeadoftheHooch #Chattanooga

items.content_text:
This week we launched the second class of the Bloomberg LSE European City Leadership Initiative convening mayors from 17 countries who collectively serve more than 12 million residents. 

Across Europe, city leaders are stepping up to tackle complex challenges – from climate adaptation and housing to digital transformation and inclusive growth. Established and led by Bloomberg Philanthropies, together with The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), the Initiative is delivered by LSE Cities in collaboration with the Hertie School in Berlin. The Initiative equips cities with the capabilities to tackle local challenges, explore new solutions and deliver results.

Kicking off the programme, mayors convened in London for an intensive classroom experience to learn evidence-backed strategies from world-class faculty, researchers, and policy leaders on how to drive performance, work across departments, mobilise collaborations, and explore solutions that deliver tangible results for citizens. 

Welcome to the second class of the Bloomberg LSE European City Leadership Initiative. We look forward to working with you over the coming months. 

To learn more, see here: https://lnkd.in/e4twWfbB
